Task 2: Crop Circles – Messages in the Fields. Questions 13-18.

initialText.title: Crop Circles – Messages in the Fields
initialText.text: In the 1980s, farmers found enormous elaborate motifs in fields of wheat, barley and oats. Crop circles were concentrated near ancient sites such as Stonehenge and Avebury. The crops sprang back intact, but farmers objected to the disruption and UFO watchers trampling their fields. New-age travellers briefly profited, but newspaper editors made the greatest use of their beauty and mystery in summer articles. In 1991, Doug Bower and Dave Chorley admitted making more than 200 circles. The article reads the circles as anonymous land-based protest art, questioning ownership and access to English land; their short-lived, uncommercialisable form is presented as a tradition of great art.

questionGroups.info: Task 3: How to Stop Overthinking. For questions 19-24 choose the sentence A-H that best fits the gap.

initialText.title: How to Stop Overthinking
initialText.text: The text explains that repetitive, unhelpful thought patterns affect mood, work, relationships and sleep. It describes mind reading, worst-case thinking and strategies for becoming aware of feelings, reframing thoughts, problem solving, writing worries down and using healthy distraction.

questionGroups.info: Task 4: How Dogs Understand Us. Complete questions 25-32.

initialText.title: How Dogs Understand Us
initialText.text: Studies suggest that dogs understand both words and emotions and interpret body language and facial expressions. The article discusses speech tone, gesture interpretation, genetics, the variation of canine cognition and its practical application in training, therapy and assistive technologies.

questionGroups.info: Task 5: What Is Intuitive Design? Complete questions 33-40 with options A-M.

initialText.title: What Is Intuitive Design?
initialText.text: The article defines intuitive design as a design users can understand and use immediately. It argues that intuitive use depends on interaction between a specific user and the design, familiar principles from other domains, and expectations of instant access in a digital environment.
